title: Chapter 5, the deep revision: Changes
draft: Chapter 05 - The Shape of Absence (Draft 4, the deep revision).md
chapter: Chapter 05 - The Shape of Absence (Draft 5, before the author's revision of 1 October).md
intro_md:
Started 29 September 2026. Chapter 5 was rewritten from the new design agreed in `Chapter 05 - Design.md` ("The deep revision"), and the rewrite is compared with the version before it, scene by scene, in `Chapter 05 - What the Deep Revision Changed.md`. Its first draft is saved unchanged as `Chapter Development/Volume 1/Chapter 05/Drafts/Chapter 05 - The Shape of Absence (Draft 4, the deep revision).md`, and every round from here is a change against it. The version before the deep revision is `Chapter Development/Volume 1/Chapter 05/Drafts/Chapter 05 - The Shape of Absence (Draft 3, before the deep revision).md`, written by `Chapter Development/Volume 1/Chapter 05/Drafts/Chapter 05 - change list.json`.

- **Round 1** (29 September, change 1): the author's note on the window and the bread: "I don't agree she should eat, and remove 'sill'. [Stop] putting buzz words."
- **Round 2** (29 September, changes 2–5): the author's review, "Several things still keep it below the level of Chapter 4": Thaer's first look at her, Leorin's first words, her plea to Thaer, and "Sometime". Its first point, italics for her thoughts, needed no change: every thought is already in italics in the file, and a plain-text copy loses them.
- **Round 3** (29 September, changes 6–11): the tray (the author: "say he was still looking at the tray, not the bread"), then the final pass the author asked for, "looking for errors, POV slips etc." The pass found no point-of-view slips, no continuity errors and no house-style faults. It found one unclear pronoun, one line that didn't fit where she was, and three repeats ("His eyes went…" four times, "Seralune looked…" twice in six lines, and a tenth "Then" that echoed the opening's "Then there were footsteps").
- **Round 4** (29 September, changes 12–14, and change 11 edited): one last pass, at the author's request ("Do one last pass to make sure"). Again no point-of-view, continuity or house-style faults. Four small repeats: two "then"s in one sentence, "next" in two paragraphs side by side, "in her lap" three times (twice in a row), and "came" in the last two one-line paragraphs, which change 11 had introduced.
- **Round 5** (29 September, changes 15–23): the author's review, "What needs work": fewer question-list thoughts and more that reason; no repeated thoughts; one moment where she adds the evidence up and stops; Seralune's line about Nereth cut; two point-of-view fixes.
- **Round 6** (29 September, changes 23–24): the blows and their stopping, in the author's words ("I still don't like these two lines… It sounds like they are doing something to it / The noises… They've stopped").
- **Round 7** (29 September, changes 25–28): after Claude's honest review. Leorin's "Forgive me, Seralune.", the recap half of her anger cut, Thaer's slip, and her fight with the door (the author's direction, options A1, B1, C1, D1 and D2).

sections.Leorin: Leorin at the foot of the stairs

changes.title: The window, without the bread
changes.before:
She got up and went to the window. The shutters still stood open, and the spray blew in cold off the falls. She leaned out as far as she dared. The wall dropped away beneath the sill, smooth and wet, all the way down to where the falls met the forest, so far below her that she couldn't see the bottom.

She stayed there until her hands were numb on the sill. Then she went back to the table, pulled the tray towards her and ate the bread. It hurt to swallow, and she ate every piece of it.

After that she sat on the bed with her back against the wall, and listened to every blow, and waited for morning, and for Thaer.
changes.after:
She got up and went to the window. The shutters still stood open, and the spray blew in cold off the falls. She leaned out as far as she dared. The wall dropped away beneath her, smooth and wet, all the way down to where the falls met the forest, so far below that she couldn't see the bottom.

She stayed there until the cold had got into her hands. Then she went back to the bed and sat with her back against the wall, and listened to every blow, and waited for morning, and for Thaer.
changes.why: The author: "I don't agree she should eat, and remove 'sill'. [Stop] putting buzz words." So she no longer eats the bread (call 14 is a no, and so is the eating agreed in round 1, question 3). She still goes to the window and looks down at the drop. "Sill" goes both times: "beneath her" says where the wall drops, and "until the cold had got into her hands" is how Chapter 4 says it ("The cold of it had got into that whole side of her face"). "You haven't eaten." and Thaer looking at the bread stay, because they're about him avoiding her, not about the food.

changes.title: "At last, he looked at her"
changes.before: At last he saw her. He went to sheathe his sword without looking, but the point missed and scraped across the plates at his hip, and he had to look down to find the sheath. She had watched him put that sword away all her life, and he had never once needed to look.
changes.after: At last, her brother looked at her. He went to sheathe his sword without looking, but the point missed and scraped across the plates at his hip, and he had to look down to find the sheath. She had watched him put that sword away all her life, and he had never once needed to look.
changes.why: The author's review: "'At last he saw her' → 'At last, he looked at her.'" It makes "look" four times in three sentences, but the first two now read as cause and effect: he looks at her at last, so he doesn't look at the sword, and misses. *Edited (29 September):* "At last, her brother looked at her." (the author's suggestion). The chapter's first "he" had nothing in the chapter to point to, and it picks up Chapter 4's last line ("fear in her brother's eyes").

changes.title: "What have you done?"
changes.before:
Then he turned to Thaer. "Thaeroval. What happened here? Why has the door been cut down?"

He was looking past them at the doorway, and at the door lying in two pieces on the floor. Then his eyes came back to the sword at Thaer's hip, and stayed there.
changes.after: Then he turned to Thaer. "Thaeroval." He looked from the ruined door to the sword at Thaer's hip. "What have you done?"
changes.why: The author's review: "Leorin's opening still asks about visible evidence… 'Thaeroval.' Leorin looked from the ruined door to the sword at his hip. 'What have you done?'" It replaces the author's own line from round 2 of the design ("What happened here? Why is the door cut down?"). Two fixes to fit the page: the narration says "He", not "Leorin", because she doesn't know him yet (she recognises him two paragraphs later); and it's "Thaer's hip", since "his hip" would read as Leorin's own. The look that followed the old question is now inside the new one, so that paragraph goes.
changes.decision_note: The author's line (29 September), with the two fixes.

changes.title: "You're all I have"
changes.before: "Did I do something wrong? Nobody will tell me anything, and you… you of all people."
changes.after: "I don't know anyone here, Thaer. You're all I have, and you won't even look at me. Did I do something wrong?"
changes.why: The author's review: "One emotional line remains generic… More personal: 'Did I do something wrong? I don't know anyone here, Thaer. You're all I have, and you won't even look at me.'" It replaces the author's own "you… you of all people". One fix: the question comes last, so that Thaer's "No.", which comes "at once", answers it. After "you won't even look at me", a bare "No." would read as him denying that. "You won't even look at me" also fits what the page shows: on the gallery "He wouldn't even look at her", and his eyes only come up to hers at his full name.
changes.decision_note: The author's line (29 September), with the question moved to the end.

changes.title: "Sometime in the night"
changes.before: Some time in the night, she felt a blow through the soles of her feet before she heard it, dull and heavy, and then another, and another, slow and steady.
changes.after: Sometime in the night, she felt a blow through the soles of her feet before she heard it, dull and heavy, and then another, and another, slow and steady.
changes.why: The author's review: "'Some time in the night' → 'Sometime in the night.'" Both forms are correct British English; the author has asked for this one twice.

changes.title: Looking at the tray
changes.before: She looked from the tray to him. He was still looking at the bread.
changes.after: She looked at him. He was still looking at the tray.
changes.why: The author: "Say he was still looking at the tray, not the bread." The line before already says "His eyes went to the tray on the table", so "She looked from the tray to him" would have made three trays in three lines; it's now "She looked at him.", and the author's sentence is word for word.

changes.title: "While he took her in"
changes.before: He let go at once, but he didn't step back. His hands stayed on her shoulders, not quite steady, while his eyes went over her: her face, the blood dried down her wrist, her bare feet on the stone. He was still breathing hard.
changes.after: He let go at once, but he didn't step back. His hands stayed on her shoulders, not quite steady, while he took her in: her face, the blood dried down her wrist, her bare feet on the stone. He was still breathing hard.
changes.why: Final pass: "His eyes went…" came four times (here, "back to the crystal", "past her to the broken doorway" and "to the tray on the table"). This is the one that can go without losing anything; the other three are agreed lines.
changes.decision_note: A craft fix from the final pass.

changes.title: "Couldn't keep still"
changes.before: Seralune couldn't sit still. She walked from the fire to the window and back again, and her legs still shook, and she walked anyway.
changes.after: Seralune couldn't keep still. She walked from the fire to the window and back again, and her legs still shook, and she walked anyway.
changes.why: Final pass: she's on her feet here (she has just caught hold of the bedpost), so "couldn't sit still" reads as though she'd been sitting.
changes.decision_note: A craft fix from the final pass.

changes.title: Whose bare feet
changes.before: The second guard looked past her at Seralune, and then down at her bare feet, and lowered his sword. "Leave it."
changes.after: The second guard looked past Nereth at Seralune, and down at her bare feet, and lowered his sword. "Leave it."
changes.why: Final pass: with "past her at Seralune", the second "her" could be Nereth's feet. Naming Nereth leaves only Seralune for "her".
changes.decision_note: A craft fix from the final pass.

changes.title: The binding
changes.before: Seralune looked down at the binding. "Thank you."
changes.after: The binding was neat and firm. "Thank you," Seralune said.
changes.why: Final pass: "Seralune looked at her." is six lines above. What she sees does the looking, and the tag keeps the speaker clear.
changes.decision_note: A craft fix from the final pass.

changes.title: The last footsteps
changes.before: Then there were footsteps in the corridor.
changes.after: There were footsteps in the corridor.
changes.why: Final pass: the chapter's tenth paragraph to start with "Then", and word for word the start of the guards' arrival ("Then there were footsteps above them"). *Edited in round 4:* it was "Footsteps came along the corridor.", which put "came" in two one-line paragraphs in a row ("Two knocks came."). It's now the plain form the first draft had, without the "Then".
changes.decision_note: A craft fix from the final pass.

changes.title: Leorin's eyes
changes.before: Nobody did. Leorin's eyes came to her then, and stayed longer than they had yet, and then went to the floor. Thaer took her arm again, and this time she was glad of it.
changes.after: Nobody did. Leorin's eyes came to her then, and stayed longer than they had yet, before they dropped to the floor. Thaer took her arm again, and this time she was glad of it.
changes.why: Last pass: two "then"s in one sentence.
changes.decision_note: A craft fix from the last pass.

changes.title: "At the corner"
changes.before: She looked back for him at the next corner. He was gone.
changes.after: She looked back for him at the corner. He was gone.
changes.why: Last pass: "at the next corner" and, straight after, "Her knees gave at the next stair."
changes.decision_note: A craft fix from the last pass.

changes.title: "From the bed"
changes.before: The blows went on. Seralune sat with her hand in her lap and listened to them, and thought of the crystal standing split open in that room far below her, and of the word that had come through the door.
changes.after: The blows went on. Seralune listened to them from the bed, and thought of the crystal standing split open in that room far below her, and of the word that had come through the door.
changes.why: Last pass: "in her lap" three times (her hands before Thaer comes back, then Nereth's, then hers here), the last two in paragraphs side by side.
changes.decision_note: A craft fix from the last pass.

changes.title: "Before he stopped too"
changes.before: She stopped walking. His hand dragged at her arm for a step before he felt it, and then he stopped too.
changes.why: Review: she can't know when he felt it.
changes.after: She stopped walking. His hand dragged at her arm for a step, and then he stopped too.

changes.title: The guards: no question list
changes.before:
*What's happening? Why are so many people here?*

Her mana crowded up under her ribs.
changes.why: Review: a thought that only asks what the prose has already shown. **This was the author's own line** (Part 1, call 4), so it's flagged.
changes.after: Her mana crowded up under her ribs.

changes.title: Leorin's age, shorter
changes.before:
*That was Leorin. It can't have been, though. Leorin isn't old.*

*But it was him, I know it was. My own cousin, bowing to me like he'd never seen me before. So why does he look so old? What happened?*
changes.why: Review: "*Leorin isn't old.* would do." The cousin line stays (the author's round 1 and C1). **Cut from the author's own lines:** *So why does he look so old? What happened?* (Part 1, call 6). *Edited (29 September):* once Leorin says "Forgive me, Seralune." (change 25), a thought about him bowing "like he'd never seen me before" ignored what he'd just said. It now reacts to it, and keeps "my own cousin" (the author's round 1).
changes.after: *Leorin isn't old. My own cousin, asking me to forgive him. For what?*

changes.title: One palace thought, not two
changes.before: *This is the palace. It has to be; I'd know the falls anywhere. So why don't I know where I am?*
changes.why: Review: *So I was in the palace after all* already says it, and the narration shows the corridors are wrong.

changes.title: The sum she won't finish
changes.before:
*How in the world did it grow so big? It was nowhere near that size this morning.*

*How long was I in that room?*

She turned to him. "Thaer, how long was I in there?"
changes.why: Review: the evidence never adds up into one moment where she reasons until it breaks, the way Chapter 4's door did ("Keeping who in? Me?"). Leorin is "white", not "grey", as the page describes him. **Cut from the author's own lines:** *How long was I in that room?*, since she asks Thaer the same thing aloud straight after.
changes.after:
*How in the world did it grow so big? It was nowhere near that size this morning.*

*A tree doesn't grow like that in a year. Leorin didn't go white in one. So it's been…*

She didn't let herself finish it.

She turned to him. "Thaer, how long was I in there?"

changes.title: The ship, unnamed for a beat
changes.before: It was a ship. She had seen ships fly before, but never one that size.
changes.why: Review: "It was a ship." was flat after the build; she fails to name it for a beat first.
changes.after: She couldn't make sense of it at first. Then the shape of it came together, and she knew it for a ship. She had seen ships fly before, but never one that size.

changes.title: Pacing, without question lists
changes.before:
*Why is he so on edge? He's never been like this, not once.*

*And those guards on the stairs, with their swords out, staring at me. What did they think I was going to do?*

*Only that old servant smiled at me. Why him, when nobody else would even look at me?*

Then there were voices outside.
changes.why: Review: all three repeat what the prose showed, and the old servant's smile is already noted on the stairs. **Cut from the author's own lines:** *Why is he so on edge? He's never been like this, not once.* (round 4 of the Chapter 4 design).
changes.after: Then there were voices outside.

changes.title: No comment on Nereth
changes.before: Seralune looked at her. *Well. At least someone in this palace says what she thinks.*
changes.why: Review: it explains Nereth straight after she's shown it. Trust the reader.

changes.title: The blows, answered
changes.before: *They're mending it, and it's for me.*
changes.after: *Whatever they're doing down there, they're doing it to that thing.*
changes.why: The author: "I still don't like these two lines, make something Alisaie would think… It sounds like they are doing something to it." The sentence before it names the crystal, so "it" is clear. Replaces N2, agreed in the dialogue round. *Edited (29 September):* the author picked option 3 of five variants.

changes.title: When the blows stop
changes.before: *They've stopped. It's mended, then.*
changes.after: *They've stopped. Whatever they were doing, it's done.*
changes.why: The author's line ("The noises… They've stopped"). Replaces O, agreed in the dialogue round. *Edited (29 September):* the author picked option 2 of five variants.

changes.title: "Forgive me, Seralune"
changes.before: Leorin stepped back against the wall to let them pass, and the guards on the stairs got out of her way.
changes.after: Leorin stepped back against the wall to let them pass. As she went by him, he said, so quietly that she barely heard it, "Forgive me, Seralune." The guards on the stairs got out of her way.
changes.why: Review point 4: Leorin was thin. The author (D2): "he says Forgive me Seralune". Her name, not "Your Highness": the cousin under the office. It doesn't say what for.

changes.title: The anger, without the recap
changes.before: "You told me to follow you, and I followed. You left me in here, and I stayed." She was on her feet now. "I sat in that room all day, Thaeroval, and nobody came. Now I want answers, and I want them now."
changes.after: She was on her feet now. "I sat in that room all day, Thaeroval, and nobody came. Now I want answers, and I want them now."
changes.why: Review point 8: the first half retold the chapter. **The author's own line** (round 4 of the Chapter 4 design), cut on the author's word (D1).

changes.title: Thaer's slip
changes.before:
"Seralune, get some rest. I'll be back in the morning."

He took her hand from his arm, gently, and looked at the cut. Then he let go of her and went to the door.
changes.after:
He turned round. "If it were up to me, you'd—" He stopped. "It isn't up to me."

His face closed again. "Seralune, get some rest. I'll be back in the morning."

He took her hand from his arm, gently, and looked at the cut. Then he let go of her and went to the door.
changes.why: The author: Thaer slips, "his love for his sister nearly takes over his duties as a Ruler and protector of Natharul" (A1). It also gives her a real piece: someone else decides, which her night thought (*Father will listen to me. He has to.*) now follows from.

changes.title: The door
changes.before:
His hand stopped on the door. Then he opened it and went out, and the lock turned.

*He didn't tell me.*
changes.after:
His hand stopped on the door. Then he opened it and went out, and the lock turned.

She ran to the door, grabbed the handle and shook it with both hands. The cut split wider, and she didn't care. "Thaer! Thaeroval, come back here! Don't you ignore me!"

His footsteps stopped.

Thaer's voice came through the door, low: "Leave her be." His footsteps went on.

*It isn't up to him. Then who is it up to?*
changes.why: The author: she runs to the door, shakes it and shouts his name, "come back here, don't ignore me" (B1, C1). His footsteps stopping is the slip a second time. "Leave her be" is why the guards stay out until her later shout, and the handle takes the blood Nereth sees afterwards. *Edited (29 September):* her thought after the door is now *It isn't up to him. Then who is it up to?* (the author's pick, option 2), replacing *He didn't tell me.*, since the slip means he did tell her one thing.
